Found under Settings, Tools, Disposable inbox.

<a id="page-inbox"></a>

## About this page

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Makes a throwaway address on a public mail service and shows the mail that arrives, for a sign-up that only needs one confirmation mail.

#### Why it is there

Some sites want an address before they show you anything. A throwaway one keeps your own address, and your aliases, out of their lists.

#### How it works

Choose mail.tm or Guerrilla Mail and click **Make an address**. Copy the address into the sign-up form, and what is sent to it appears under **Arrived**.

When you leave the page, WM Pass forgets the address and the key to its mailbox. You cannot open that inbox again.

#### When to use it

For a one-off, such as a download link or a trial. Never for an account you want to keep: a password reset would go to an inbox you can no longer open.

#### Limits

The service, and possibly others, can read what arrives. Treat anything sent there as public.

WM Pass does not delete the mailbox when you leave. It stays at the service, under that service's own rules.

Needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

#### On Android

Makes throwaway addresses on a mail service and keeps each one, with its mail, until you close it. For sign-ups that only need a confirmation mail.

Tap **New address** and choose where it comes from: mail.tm, mail.gw or Guerrilla Mail, your own server running the mail.tm API, or an Inbucket server you run. Give it a name if you like, so you know what it was for.

Each address stays in the list, saved inside the encrypted vault, like a chat in a chat app. Open one to copy the address and read what arrived.

Tap a mail to read it as a mail app shows it, with its layout and links. Pictures stay unloaded until you tap **Load**. A code in it gets its own copy button, and the note button at the top saves the mail to the vault.

The bin button closes the address. Where the service allows, it can delete the mailbox there too; Guerrilla Mail clears its own within the hour.

The service, and possibly others, can read what arrives. Treat anything sent there as public.

Plain http works only for this phone and Tailscale addresses, so a server of your own needs https anywhere else.

Needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

See also [mail.tm](/guide/settings/inbox/#concept-inbox-mailtm), [Guerrilla Mail](/guide/settings/inbox/#concept-inbox-guerrilla), [Email aliases](/guide/settings/aliases/).

<a id="concept-inbox-mailtm"></a>

## mail.tm

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

A free mailbox service. WM Pass makes a new account there for each address.

#### How it works

WM Pass asks api.mail.tm which domains it offers, then creates a mailbox with a random name and a random password, and signs in to it. Nothing about you is in either.

While the page is open, it asks api.mail.tm for new mail with the sign-in key. Opening a mail fetches its full text.

See also [Disposable inbox](/guide/settings/inbox/), [Guerrilla Mail](/guide/settings/inbox/#concept-inbox-guerrilla).

<a id="concept-inbox-guerrilla"></a>

## Guerrilla Mail

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

A free throwaway mail service that hands out an address with no account.

#### How it works

WM Pass asks api.guerrillamail.com for an address and gets a session key with it, which it sends with each check for new mail.

Its API wants an IP address and a program name with every call, so WM Pass sends 127.0.0.1 and "WM-Pass" instead of anything real.

Opening a mail shows the opening lines that came with the list, not the whole message.

#### Limits

Those fixed values keep your real address out of the request itself. The service still sees where the connection comes from.

See also [Disposable inbox](/guide/settings/inbox/), [mail.tm](/guide/settings/inbox/#concept-inbox-mailtm).

<a id="group-inbox-arrived"></a>

## Arrived

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

The mail sent to the address so far. Click one to read it below the list.

#### How it works

The page asks the service for new mail every 8 seconds while it is open.

Mail is shown as plain text only, so no picture, tracking pixel or script in it ever loads or runs here.

#### On Android

The mail sent to this address, newest first. A dot marks what came in since you opened the page. Tap one to read it.

The page asks the service for new mail every 8 seconds while it is open, and the refresh button asks now.

A mail opens with its own layout, but no script in it runs, it cannot reach anything on the phone, and pictures load only when you tap **Load**, so the sender cannot tell you opened it. Links open in your browser.

See also [Disposable inbox](/guide/settings/inbox/).
